$comment: C 6.7p2 (D-CSUBSET-DECL-QUALIFIER-BEFORE-STORAGE-CLASS, P65 + residue (2) of D-CSUBSET-DECL-GRAMMAR-LOW-RESIDUES): the declaration specifiers are an UNORDERED set, so a TYPE QUALIFIER may be written BEFORE the storage-class specifiers. Every declaration here writes the qualifier first — `const static int`, `volatile static int`, `const register int`, `const typedef int`, `static const inline`, `const auto` — each of which was `error[P_NoAlternativeMatched] … got 'static'` (or the equivalent) before this cycle, and each of which gcc 13.3.0 (-std=c2x), clang 18.1.3 (-std=c23) and MSVC 19.51.36252 accept and RUN, probed SEPARATELY one translation unit at a time. THE EXAMPLE TESTS MEANING, NOT PARSING: a leading qualifier lands in the declaration's specifier PREFIX (the subtree every positional consumer STRIPS) instead of in the type head, so each arm gates on a RUNTIME consequence — internal linkage, a real volatile load/store the release pipeline cannot fold, block-scope STATIC STORAGE DURATION proved by two calls returning 1 then 2, a working typedef alias, and a mutable pointer to const. exit = 42. RED-ON-DISABLE (REMOVE direction): delete "headQualifier" from the trailing {repeat} of `declSpecifiers` and from both alternatives of `localDeclSpecifiers` in c.lang.json — every declaration becomes a loud parse error and the example never links.
